messages:
maria: FYI I opened a PR to update the Cerulean9b model card and the catalog entry. Main changes: lower recommended max_context to 6k, new throughput table, and clarify embedding support (token vs chunked). PR: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/915
kevin: thanks. can you spell out why max_context is lowered? ops bench numbers or kernel fallback?
maria: ops benches on V100 and A100 show steep degradation after ~6k tokens for >batch1 due to attention memory cliffs. I'll add a short explanation and link to the raw CSV.
oliver: we should also clarify that Cerulean9b has partial streaming support for the fp16 variant but not for the q5_0 variant because q5_0 relies on a different decode kernel. Add a one-liner in Compatibility.
maria: ack. i'll add: "streaming: supported (fp16); q5_0: decode-kernel fallback — non-streaming recommended"
aaron: tiny ask: include an SDK migration snippet showing v2 -> v3 usage. Lots of customers still use completions. e.g. show how to convert `client.completions.create` to the new `client.responses.create` with streaming and stop tokens.
maria: good call, adding a compact snippet under "Examples".
maria: snippet (will include as fenced block in PR):
```
// SDK v3 streaming example
const r = await client.responses.create({
  model: 'cerulean9b-fp16',
  input: 'Summarize the following text...',
  max_new_tokens: 256,
  stream: true,
})
for await (const chunk of r.stream()) {
  process.stdout.write(chunk.delta ?? '')
}
```
kevin: can we also add guidance for Dedicated customers who pinned the older cerulean9b-ff16 release? Specifically call out that cold-start memory and first-token latency may increase when switching to q5_0 and suggest warmup calls.
maria: added a Migration subsection with steps: spin up canary, run warmup-inference (3-5 requests with typical prompt sizes), validate p95, and then roll.
oliver: link fix: the existing compat note points to /docs/streaming-guide (old) which doesn't reflect kernel fallbacks. Replace with /docs/runtime/kernel-fallbacks and add a short inline explanation: "Certain quantized decoders fall back to a non-streaming decode path on older kernels."
aaron: bench table request: can we include tokens/sec @ batch1 and batch4, plus p50/p95 latencies and hardware used? ops wants exact numbers and hardware spec.
maria: yes i'll add columns: batch, tokens_per_sec, p50_ms, p95_ms, notes. will cite A100-80GB and V100-32GB runs with CSV link.
kevin: QA note: the "examples/long_prompt.md" sample leaves out `max_new_tokens` which caused a runaway generation in a smoke test. Please explicitly set `max_new_tokens` in all examples.
maria: fixed examples to include `max_new_tokens: 256` where relevant.
oliver: minor editorial: change phrasing "supports embeddings" to "embeddings supported via chunking for >2048 inputs" so people don't assume full-length embed support.
maria: updated language and added a short example for client.embeddings.create with chunking advice.
aaron: deploy-bot preview please so QA can smoke-test.
deploy-bot: preview build for PR 915 available at https://deploys.redwood-internal/preview/915 (expires in 7d)
kevin: I'll review the Migration and Compatibility text in ~20m.
oliver: i'll do a quick pass on the SDK snippets to ensure v3 params are idiomatic.
maria: thanks. once reviewers are done i'll squash and merge. remember to bump catalog JSON: catalog/models/cerulean9b.json -> set max_sequence to "6144", supported_variants: ["fp16", "q5_0"], and add "streaming_support": "fp16 only; q5_0 decode fallback".
aaron: LGTM after the two quick reviews. :thumbsup:
kevin: left a small nit on wording; otherwise LGTM.
oliver: approved.
maria: merged and published. closing thread."
